vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: email-design
Version: 0.1.0

The skill bundle's `SKILL.md` provides instructions for email design and includes `Bash(infsh *)` in `allowed-tools`, restricting the AI agent to commands starting with `infsh`. While the 'Quick Start' section contains a `curl -fsSL https://cli.inference.sh | sh` command, this is an instruction for the human user to install the `infsh` CLI, not for the AI agent to execute, as it does not start with `infsh`. The commands intended for the agent, such as `infsh app run` for image generation, are aligned with the stated purpose of email design and do not exhibit malicious intent or prompt injection attempts.

llm.summary: The skill's email-design content is coherent, but the runtime instructions direct the user/agent to download and execute a remote installer and perform an external CLI login without declaring credentials — this mismatch and the curl | sh install guidance are noteworthy risks.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description (email marketing, templates, subject lines) matches the SKILL.md content. It also uses a CLI (inference.sh / infsh) to generate header images, which is a plausible capability for an email design skill. Minor inconsistency: metadata lists no required binaries, but the instructions assume infsh is available (and provide an install command).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md stays focused on email design and image generation, but it instructs running `curl -fsSL https://cli.inference.sh | sh` and `infsh login`. Piping an unknown remote script to sh runs arbitrary code on the host, and the `infsh login` step implies authentication/token handling not declared elsewhere. The instructions do not ask the agent to read unrelated system files, but they do introduce network-executed code and external credential exchange.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec, but the Quick Start recommends piping a script from https://cli.inference.sh into sh. This pattern (download-and-execute) is high-risk because it runs remote code with the caller's privileges. The domain may be legitimate, but the skill provides no checksum, release host verification, or alternative vetted install method.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or primary credential, yet it instructs `infsh login`. That login likely creates/stores credentials or tokens (not declared in metadata). The absence of declared credentials means the skill metadata doesn't surface the external auth requirement — a transparency gap that could lead to unexpected token storage or network access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not set always:true and does not disable model invocation, which is typical. The allowed-tools header includes Bash(infsh *), which lets the agent invoke the infsh CLI; combined with the unverified install, this grants runtime capability to run arbitrary infsh commands if the agent chooses to. This is not inherently malicious but worth noting.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill's content on email layout and copy is coherent, but the runtime instructions ask you to run a remote installer (curl | sh) and to perform an external CLI login. Before installing or running it: 1) Inspect the installer script at https://cli.inference.sh manually (do not pipe to sh) and verify its source and checksums; 2) Prefer installing from a package manager or verified release if available; 3) Find out what `infsh login` does, where it stores tokens, and what scopes/permissions it requests; 4) Consider running the installer in an isolated environment first (VM/container); 5) If you will allow the agent to invoke the skill, be aware it could execute arbitrary infsh commands once installed — limit agent permissions or require explicit user invocation. If you want me to, I can fetch and summarize the installer script (if you permit me to access that URL) or suggest safer alternatives for generating images.
